title: The Tantraloka
author: abhinavagupta
attributionNote: Written by Abhinavagupta, who names himself and his teachers in its closing chapters. The verses are supported by his own prose commentary, the Tantralokaviveka.
description: The Tantraloka is the great summary of Kashmir Shaiva tantra: in thirty-seven chapters (ahnikas) it sets out the nature of the absolute as consciousness and its freedom, the means of knowledge and the hierarchy of the tattvas, initiation and the transmission of doctrine, ritual, the ways of individual and universal experience, and finally the recognition in which the world is known as Shiva's own play.
historicalContext: Abhinavagupta's synthesis gathered the tantric lineages of Kashmir into one philosophical system, and the Tantraloka became its authoritative statement — read in the twentieth century, alongside his commentaries, as one of the most elaborate accounts of consciousness in any Indian tradition.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit verses of all thirty-seven ahnikas, with the auto-commentary interleaved as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one ahnika at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
